headline: High-risk git/workspace collision and prompt-injection exposure: Aider’s shared repo writes can corrupt Rasa-driven workflows, while compliance risk is limited by sparse residency data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and can ingest file content as context; if Rasa outputs are copied into the shared repo or another bridged channel, attacker-controlled text could steer Aider. Rasa’s documented chat channels make such bridging plausible, but no direct shared channel is shown, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Rasa output is copied into the shared git workspace or another file Aider reads
IF Aider is configured to treat repository text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Keep Rasa transcripts out of the shared repo
Use a separate review-only workspace for bot outputs
Add a prompt-injection filter before copying text into Aider
Require manual approval for any instruction-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between bot output and code editor

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history in a shared repo, so any sensitive text placed there can be read by Aider. Rasa handles text/voice and can expose conversation content through messaging integrations. The pair therefore has a plausible shared-workspace leakage path, but the profiles do not show direct automatic exfiltration, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive customer text is stored in the shared repository
IF Rasa conversation logs are exported into files Aider can read
mitigations: Store bot logs outside the code repo
Restrict Aider to non-sensitive branches
Redact PII before exporting conversations
Rotate any secrets found in repo history
requires-engineering: separate storage and access controls for bot logs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared git-repo state across instances; Rasa is a multi-instance chatbot framework with allowlisted network egress. If both operate on the same repo or mutable workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The overlap is directly documented for Aider and inferred for the pair, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git repository or workspace
IF Rasa or its integrations modify files that Aider also edits
mitigations: Run the agents in separate repos
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable auto-commit during concurrent runs
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can generate code or repo changes that Rasa may consume indirectly if its outputs are copied into support workflows or automation. Rasa’s dialogue system can then act on those outputs without a verification step. Because the profiles do not show a direct action-taking chain, the risk is real but not high.
conditions: IF Aider-generated text is forwarded into Rasa as authoritative content
IF Rasa automation acts on that content without human review
mitigations: Require human review before forwarding Aider output
Add validation rules for any code or facts passed to Rasa
Keep Aider output in a draft-only channel
Log and diff all forwarded messages
requires-engineering: add verification gates between generation and action

E_compliance.rationale: Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys and git history, while Rasa handles text/voice and messaging integrations. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern is visible: if regulated data is placed into Aider’s repo or provider calls, policy gaps could arise. The other agent is not cited because no specific mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repo or sent through Aider provider calls
IF Rasa conversations contain data subject to stricter retention rules than the repo
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the repo
Redact transcripts before storage
Confirm retention settings for bot logs
Limit provider keys to least privilege
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
